name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.56M km² and Antarctic 1.47M km² below average on 9 Nov; neither at a record low
state: On 9 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 8.66 million km², about 1.56 million below the 1981–2010 average and fourth-lowest for the date. Antarctic extent was 15.27 million km², about 1.47 million below average and second-lowest for the date (NSIDC). Both are past the −1.0 million Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low for the date.
for_you: Low sea ice mainly affects polar ecosystems, Arctic communities and shipping routes, and adds to longer-term warming. There is no direct short-term effect on most readers.
rubric_hit: Arctic −1.56M km² and Antarctic −1.47M km², below −1.0M Watch line; no record low

sources.title: NSIDC — Sea Ice Index tools (daily extent and anomaly)

why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
